companies.note: No CMO or VP Marketing is listed anywhere on Ramp's own pages (checked ramp.com/careers, the ramp.com/authors executive pages and the leadership coverage, 6 Sep 2026). Marketing has sat inside co-founder Karim Atiyeh's remit (risk, operations and marketing) rather than under a marketing officer. IMPORTANT for the desk: the brief's decision-maker is out of date — Eric Glyman is now CO-CEO alongside Atiyeh (announced Jul 2026). Also: no F1 or motorsport programme could be found for Ramp. Two searches across 2026 F1 team partner lists and the Visa Cash App Racing Bulls sponsor roster returned nothing; Visa is the VCARB title partner and renewed to 2030. What Ramp DOES have is a dedicated sports-sponsorship function (Mason Melnick) buying US properties — Stanford Athletics, SMU Athletics, The Snow League. So Ramp is a proven sponsorship buyer with no motorsport asset yet, which is a stronger opening than a halo pitch, but the brief's F1 claim should be corrected before it goes out.

people.name: Mason Melnick
people.note: THE call. Ramp has no CMO, but it has a named person whose whole job is buying sports sponsorship — rare at this stage and the single most useful contact in this batch. He is quoted by name in SMU Athletics' July 2026 partnership announcement, and Ramp's sports portfolio under him runs to Stanford Athletics (official expense-management partner) and The Snow League (exclusive corporate card and preferred fintech partner, multi-season). All US, all non-motorsport: a three-year F1/FE deal would be his first European and first motorsport property.

people.name: Colin Kennedy
people.note: Owns operations, partnerships, corporate development and sales — announced on Ramp's own blog. Ran partnerships globally for Stripe before Ramp, so he reads a multi-year partnership on commercial terms rather than brand terms. The co-signer on anything Melnick brings forward.

people.name: Karim Atiyeh
people.note: Elevated from CTO to co-CEO in July 2026. Before the title change he personally oversaw risk, operations AND marketing — i.e. he is the de facto marketing owner as well as a cheque signer. Pitch him and you are pitching the marketing function.

people.name: Eric Glyman
people.note: The brief names him 'CEO & Co-Founder'. Still there, still a founder, but as of Jul 2026 he shares the top job — the desk should say co-CEO. He wrote the announcement post himself.

companies.note: The CMO seat is VACANT and that is the finding. Annie Shea Weckesser, SambaNova's CMO, left in December 2025 to become SVP and Chief Marketing & Communications Officer at Intel (Intel newsroom, 15 Dec 2025). No successor has been announced and none appears on sambanova.ai/company/team; the 2026 executive announcements SambaNova has made were a CFO (Matt Padfield) and an EVP Software (Rich Heaton), not a CMO. Practical consequence for the desk: there is no marketing buyer to call — a sponsorship pitch has to go through the CRO or the CEO, and a big brand commitment is unlikely to be signed while the seat is open. Worth re-checking in a quarter. Brief's named decision-maker (Rodrigo Liang) is correct and current.

people.name: Harry Ault
people.note: With the CMO seat empty, the CRO is the effective owner of any brand or partnership spend — at SambaNova the revenue office has historically carried the marketing teams as well. Announced by SambaNova's own account (Dec 2024). Predecessor Richard Halkett's CRO remit was explicitly defined as sales, sales ops, revenue ops, customer engineering AND marketing, which is the shape of the seat.

people.name: Clyde Hosein
people.note: The operator between the CEO and the revenue org; a three-year commitment of this size goes across his desk.

people.name: Rodrigo Liang
people.note: Confirmed still Co-Founder & CEO — the brief is right. With no CMO in post he is unusually close to brand decisions. No motorsport tie found in his background (ex-Oracle SPARC engineering leadership).

companies.note: Saronic does have a real CMO, and she is a serious brand operator rather than a demand-gen hire — that matters for a sponsorship conversation. Company pages (saronic.com/team) are behind the session's egress block, so names and titles were taken from the executives' own profiles and corroborating profiles; treat as reported, and re-read the team page before an approach. Brief's named decision-maker (Dino Mavrookas) is correct. Note the constraint the desk should weigh: Saronic is a defence-autonomy company selling to the US Navy and allied navies, so a consumer-facing motorsport programme is a recruiting and prestige play (MODE B), not a customer-acquisition one.

people.name: Emily Shanklin
people.note: The buyer, and the strongest marketing CV in this batch. 15 years at SpaceX leading marketing and communications — an Emmy-winning team, reporting to Gwynne Shotwell and Elon Musk — then SVP Marketing at Luminar Technologies (automotive lidar) before Saronic. Luminar puts her one step from the automotive/motorsport world; she has run exactly the kind of hardware-spectacle brand programme an F1/FE partnership would be. No direct motorsport deal found in her history.

people.name: Rob Lehman
people.note: Owns the commercial side as a co-founder — the counter-signature on a multi-year deal.

people.name: Dino Mavrookas
people.note: Confirmed still CEO — the brief is right. Former US Navy SEAL; fronts Saronic's funding and programme announcements.

companies.note: Supabase publishes no leadership or executive page at all — it is an open-source, developer-led company and the nearest thing to a public org chart is the blog author list. There is no CMO and no VP Marketing: marketing sits with the Head of Developer Relations and Marketing, and the open roles the company is hiring are product-marketing managers, not a marketing officer. Because there is no company page of record, the people below are sourced to first-person announcements and credible secondaries and are all marked reported — re-confirm before an approach. The brief names no decision-maker for Supabase; the answer is Paul Copplestone (co-founder and CEO), with Craig Cannon as the marketing owner. Read across: a developer-brand company like this buys sponsorship as developer reach and recruiting, so the pitch is audience and content, not hospitality.

people.name: Craig Cannon
people.role: Head of Developer Relations and Marketing
people.note: The marketing owner, in seat since June 2024 — announced by himself, which is the only first-hand source that exists since Supabase has no team page. Ex-Director of Marketing and Director of Content at Y Combinator, where he built the podcast and YouTube channel: a content and audience operator, so a motorsport pitch to him has to carry a content and developer-audience argument.

people.name: Paul Copplestone
people.note: The cheque signer, and the person the brief should be naming — it currently names nobody. Known for running marketing decisions personally and publicly (launch weeks, open-source brand); a founder-led brand call is realistic here.

people.name: Ant Wilson
people.note: Technical counterpart if the deal is argued as a real engineering workstream (a team's data platform) rather than branding.

companies.note: Cleanest decision path in the batch: TENEX names its whole executive bench on its own site and announced a CMO on its own newsroom in June 2026. Brief's named decision-maker (Eric Foster) is correct and current. Worth noting that the CMO hire post-dates the $27M Series A — this is a company that has just staffed up to spend on brand, which is the moment a multi-year sponsorship is actually buyable.

people.name: Richard Rogers
people.note: THE call, and a fresh one — appointed 4 June 2026 with an explicit mandate to accelerate GLOBAL growth, i.e. hired to take a US security brand international. 25+ years across cybersecurity, AI, cloud and enterprise software; came from the CMO seat at ExtraHop. A new CMO with a global brief and new funding is the ideal buyer profile for a three-year European property. No motorsport tie found.

people.name: Edwin Solis
people.note: Co-founder owning revenue; ex-VP at Google Cloud. Named in TENEX's own Series A announcement.

people.name: Eric Foster
people.note: Confirmed still CEO — the brief is right. Three-decade security career, three-time CISO, co-founder of Cyderes and former President of Stairwell.

companies.note: No CMO: the top marketing seat is a VP of Marketing & Communications (checked tensorwave.com/about and the marketing org, 6 Sep 2026), which is normal for a company this young. Brief's named decision-maker (Darrick Horton) is correct and current. The commercial owner carries a Chief Growth Officer title rather than CRO, so growth and brand argue together here — useful, because a sponsorship can be framed as pipeline rather than pure brand.

people.name: Navi Ganancial
people.note: The marketing owner and the person to call — no CMO sits above her. In seat since July 2025, leads a small marketing team. Background is events and audience-building (co-founder of FounderMade, acquired by Tarsus in 2021; earlier Google and SC Johnson), and she has run TensorWave's CES presence — someone who already thinks in live-event activation, which is the shape of a race-weekend programme.

people.name: Jeff Tatarchuk
people.note: Growth rather than a classic CRO — the commercial counterpart on any deal, and the one who will want the pipeline argument.

people.name: Piotr Tomasik
people.note: Operator between the founders and the functions; a three-year commitment clears through him.

people.name: Darrick Horton
people.note: Confirmed still Co-Founder & CEO — the brief is right. Las Vegas-based; TensorWave is an AMD-GPU cloud, so a technical partnership story would run through the compute pitch, not the brand pitch.

companies.note: No Chief Marketing Officer is listed on threatlocker.com/company (checked 6 Sep 2026); the senior marketing seat is an SVP of Brand Marketing, and the top of the go-to-market org is the CRO. Brief's named decision-maker (Danny Jenkins) is correct and current. The useful read for the desk: ThreatLocker is already a heavy brand spender — it runs national-scale creative (the 'Zero Trust' campaign published Feb 2026, directed by Kevin O'Brien) and its own Zero Trust World conference — so this is a company that buys big brand programmes, just not through a CMO title. No motorsport sponsorship found in its portfolio.

people.name: Aliona Groh
people.note: The buyer. Brand — not demand-gen — is explicitly her remit, and she owned ThreatLocker's Feb 2026 'Zero Trust' campaign, a professionally-directed brand film. That is exactly the budget line a motorsport programme competes for, so she is the right first call. Prior: Managing Director, Growth Marketing at Allari; earlier Adacel Technologies, Embraer and Lennar — aerospace/aviation-adjacent, no motorsport tie found.

people.name: Shane Deegan
people.note: Top of the go-to-market org with no CMO above the brand SVP, so he is effectively the commercial owner of a brand commitment this size.

people.name: Danny Jenkins
people.note: Confirmed still CEO & Co-Founder — the brief is right. British-born, founder-led company of ~700 people across five continents from Orlando; fronts the brand personally, which shortens the path on a signature brand decision.

companies.note: No CMO: marketing tops out at an SVP & Head of Marketing (checked together.ai/about-us and the 2026 executive listings). Brief's named decision-maker (Vipul Ved Prakash) is correct and current. One caution the desk should carry: the commercial titles at Together AI are reported inconsistently across sources — Arielle Fidel appears as VP Strategic Partnerships and as VP Sales & Business Development, and Meicheng Shi is finance (SVP/VP Strategic Finance), NOT the CRO some directories claim. Confirm the commercial seat by phone before an approach rather than trusting a directory.

people.name: Prem Prakash
people.note: The buyer — the most senior marketing person, with no CMO above him. Ex-Head of Product Marketing at Databricks and ran marketing for Azure AI services at Microsoft: an enterprise product marketer, so a sponsorship pitch to him needs a developer/enterprise-audience argument rather than a hospitality one. No motorsport tie found.

people.name: Arielle Fidel
people.role: VP, Strategic Partnerships (also listed as VP Sales & Business Development)
people.note: The partnerships route in, at Together since Aug 2023. Ex-Director of Business Development at Twitter — she has bought and structured brand partnerships before, which is the relevant experience. Title varies by source; verify on contact.

people.name: Vipul Ved Prakash
people.note: Confirmed still Co-Founder & CEO — the brief is right.

companies.note: No CMO and no VP Marketing anywhere on TwelveLabs' own pages (checked twelvelabs.io/about-us, 6 Sep 2026) — the company is research- and founder-led, and marketing sits inside a co-founder's go-to-market remit. Brief's named decision-maker (Jae Lee) is correct and current. Strategic read the desk should not miss: TwelveLabs builds video-understanding AI, so a race series is not a logo opportunity for them — it is a data and product opportunity (searchable race footage, automated highlights, broadcast metadata). That makes the CTO a genuine counterpart, not a courtesy contact, and makes this the rare MODE-A technical case in the batch.

people.name: Soyoung Lee
people.role: Co-Founder & Head of Go-to-Market (also listed as Head of Business Development)
people.note: Listed under marketing because she is the closest thing to a marketing owner — the title is go-to-market and business development, NOT marketing, and no marketing officer exists above her. Treat as the entry point, not as a CMO.

people.name: Yoon Kim
people.note: The seniority to structure a multi-year deal and the background to see the media angle: former CTO of SK Telecom, and before that at Apple (joined via the Novauris acquisition, where he was CEO) leading speech recognition for Siri. Splits his time between San Francisco and Seoul — a partnership with an Asia-facing team or race would land with him.

people.name: Jae Lee
people.note: Confirmed still Co-Founder & CEO — the brief is right.

people.name: Aiden Lee
people.note: The technical counterpart who has to want it. If the pitch is a real workstream — video search and automated highlight generation over a team's or series' footage archive — he is the person who validates it.

companies.note: Public company (NYSE: PATH) with a proper marketing officer, and the brief's named contact is right: Michael Atalla is CMO, appointed 25 Aug 2025 and confirmed on UiPath's own newsroom and investor-relations releases. Two things the desk should correct or watch. (1) MOTORSPORT: no UiPath Formula 1 partnership could be found — not with Williams, not with any team. Williams' title partner is Atlassian (from 2025) and UiPath does not appear on any 2026 F1 team or series partner list; the historical Williams-era claim could not be substantiated from any source in this session. Do NOT put a Williams tie in front of the MD without re-checking it. (2) EMEA: no President or GM EMEA is currently named. The last publicly announced EMEA lead was Mark Gibbs (SVP & Managing Director, EMEA, appointed Sep 2022) and that could not be confirmed as current, so it is deliberately not listed here; the named regional executive is Ben Fiechtner, President Americas — wrong region for a European series. Confirm the EMEA seat before routing a European proposal.

people.name: Michael Atalla
people.note: THE call, and the brief has him right. Owns all of global marketing — brand, performance, demand generation and communications. Ex-SVP and Head of Worldwide Marketing at F5 for four years, and nearly 15 years at Microsoft where he led the Office-to-Office 365 transition. A brand-and-repositioning CMO, hired in Aug 2025 to carry UiPath's agentic-AI repositioning: a big brand platform is on-thesis for him. No motorsport buying history found.

people.name: Daniel Dines
people.note: Confirmed still Founder & CEO in 2026. Romanian founder of a NYSE-listed company with deep European roots — relevant colour for a European-series pitch.

people.name: Raghu Malpani
people.note: Expanded from CTO to Chief Product and Technology Officer effective 25 Mar 2026. The counterpart if the deal is argued as a genuine automation workstream inside a race team (garage and factory process automation) rather than as branding.

companies.note: No CMO, but there is a real marketing owner one rung down: a VP of Global Marketing. Zenity's own careers pages (zenity.io/careers) repeatedly name the 'VP of Global Marketing' as the hiring manager for its marketing roles, confirming the seat exists; the person's name is not published on zenity.io/company, so it is carried here as reported. Brief's named decision-maker (Ben Kliger) is correct and current. Two things that matter for timing: no CRO is listed, and as of Sep 2026 Zenity was still HIRING a Head of EMEA (London-based, remote) — so there is no European commercial lead in post yet. A Europe-facing motorsport programme would arrive ahead of the region it is meant to support; either wait for that hire or route it through the VP Global Marketing and the CEO.

people.name: Cinthia Portugal
people.note: The buyer — most senior marketing person, no CMO above her. Her seat is corroborated by Zenity's own job postings, which list the VP of Global Marketing as the hiring manager and interviewer for marketing roles; the name itself comes from her professional profile rather than a Zenity page, so confirm on contact. No motorsport tie found.

people.name: Ben Kliger
people.note: Confirmed still Co-Founder & CEO — the brief is right. Israeli-founded company (with Michael Bargury); ex-Microsoft. With no CRO and no EMEA lead in post, he is closer to a deal of this size than the org chart suggests.

people.name: Michael Bargury
people.note: Co-founder and the company's public technical voice (Black Hat / DEF CON research on AI-agent security). The counterpart if a team's own AI-agent security is the workstream.
